messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — onboarding 3 seed accounts into eu-central-4 + me-south1. We need accelerator quota bumps (p5 + g5), ENI increases, and egress/NAT capacity. Putting the ask here so we can open AWS cases in parallel.

raj: Can you drop account IDs and the per-account targets?

maria: Sure — accounts and target accelerators below. Also we found NATGW EIP limits are tight for our burst pool.
- 123456789012: p5: 8 -> request 24, g5: 16 -> request 48, ENIs: 500 -> request 1200
- 210987654321: p5: 4 -> request 12, g5: 8 -> request 24, ENIs: 300 -> request 800
- 345678901234: p5: 2 -> request 8, g5: 4 -> request 16, ENIs: 200 -> request 600
We also need guidance on NAT gateway EIP pool and an IPv6 fallback plan for cold/edge pools.

infra-ops: OK. Priorities look reasonable for seed ramp. Two immediate notes: 1) ask for "Accelerator (P5)" and "Accelerator (G5)" quota names separately in the EC2 quotas console, give per-region totals (not per-AZ). 2) ask ENI/quota for "Network interfaces per EC2 instance" and "Elastic IPs" / NAT gateway scaling as separate support items.

infra-ops: Suggested quota request text (copy to AWS Support case):
```
We are Redwood Inference requesting quota increases for production seed accounts. Region: eu-central-4 (and me-south1). 
Account IDs: 123456789012, 210987654321, 345678901234. 
Requested changes (per account):
- P5 accelerators (p5): increase to 24 / 12 / 8 respectively.
- G5 accelerators (g5): increase to 48 / 24 / 16 respectively.
- VPC ENI / Elastic Network Interfaces quota: increase total ENIs to 1200 / 800 / 600 respectively.
- Elastic IP quota: increase by 50 per account (for NAT GW pool & failover).
Rationale: onboarding latency-sensitive inference workloads. We will reserve capacity for dedicated pools and need predictable egress (NAT) IPs for allowlists. Please advise if they can be processed as a bulk multi-account request or need separate cases.
```

sara: Add networking notes: eu-central-4 subnets are short on available /24s in our current AZ plans. If we request lots of ENIs we also need to reserve additional secondary IP ranges or request larger subnets. For NAT: recommend provisioning a small EIP reservoir (50) and enable autoscaling NAT (multiple NAT GWs + route priority). For IPv6 fallback for cold pools, use an egress-only IGW + allowlist approach — avoids EIP scarcity for read-only telemetry.

raj: Cost/capacity check — increasing P5/G5 that much will spike commit costs if we leave reserved warm pools. Can we do staged bump? e.g., approve initial 40% now, rest as capacity fills?

infra-ops: Good call. I'll request staged increases: phase 1 = 40% of target with ability to re-open case for immediate bump. Put that in the support text as a follow-up option. Also ask AWS to confirm if these can be "accelerator entitlement" lifts vs manual limit checks (speeds up approvals).

maria: Updated support text with staged ask; I'll open cases now for all three accounts and share numbers.

devops-bot: quota-bot created support case #Q-6123456789 for account 123456789012 (eu-central-4). ETA: 48-72h.

quota-bot: Support cases opened for the other two accounts: #Q-6123456790 (210987654321) and #Q-6123456791 (345678901234). Noted staged approval request.

infra-ops: Once we get approval, reminder to update terraform module defaults: accelerator_count, eni_targets, nat_eip_pool_size so bootstrap respects new ceilings. Also add a preflight check to fail fast when subnets don't have enough secondary IP ranges.

maria: Thanks — I'll track case IDs in the onboarding doc and loop in security for allowlist prep.

quota-bot: AWS response (auto): initial review started. They may ask for justification docs or usage patterns (sustained vs burst). Keep deployment plans handy.

maria: Copy — will attach perf curves and expected steady-state concurrency. Will follow up with subnet expansion plan. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
